title: Defining the Derivative
lead: The derivative of a function at a point is defined as the limit of a difference quotient, the slope of a secant line whose second point closes in on the first. The same limit is the slope of the tangent line, an instantaneous velocity and, in general, an instantaneous rate of change.
objectives: Recognize the meaning of the tangent to a curve at a point.
Calculate the slope of a tangent line.
Identify the derivative as the limit of a difference quotient.
Calculate the derivative of a given function at a point.
Describe the velocity as a rate of change.
Explain the difference between average velocity and instantaneous velocity.
Estimate the derivative from a table of values.
summary_html:
• The slope of the tangent line to a curve measures the instantaneous rate of change of a curve. We can calculate it by finding the limit of the difference quotient or the difference quotient with increment $h.$
  • The derivative of a function $\kf(x)$ at a value $a$ is found using either of the definitions for the slope of the tangent line.
  • Velocity is the rate of change of position. As such, the velocity $\kv(t)$ at time $t$ is the derivative of the position $\ks(t)$ at time $t.$ Average velocity is given by $$\kv_{\text{ave}}=\frac{\ks(t)-\ks(a)}{t-a}.$$ Instantaneous velocity is given by $$\kv(a)=\ksprime(a)=\lim_{t\to a}\frac{\ks(t)-\ks(a)}{t-a}.$$
  • We may estimate a derivative by using a table of values.

For the following exercises, use the limit definition of derivative to show that the derivative does not exist at $x=a$ for each of the given functions.

$f(x)=x^{1/3},x=0$

For the following exercises, use the limit definition of derivative to show that the derivative does not exist at $x=a$ for each of the given functions.

$f(x)=x^{2/3},x=0$

answer.solution: Use the definition of the derivative at $a=0$ with $f(0)=0:$ $\frac{f(x)-f(0)}{x-0}=\frac{x^{2/3}}{x}=\frac{1}{x^{1/3}}.$ As $x\to 0^{+},$ $x^{1/3}\to 0^{+},$ so $\lim_{x\to 0^{+}}\frac{1}{x^{1/3}}=+\infty;$ as $x\to 0^{-},$ $x^{1/3}\to 0^{-},$ so $\lim_{x\to 0^{-}}\frac{1}{x^{1/3}}=-\infty.$ The one-sided limits are infinite and of opposite signs, so $\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{f(x)-f(0)}{x-0}$ does not exist, and $f^{\prime}(0)$ does not exist.

For the following exercises, use the limit definition of derivative to show that the derivative does not exist at $x=a$ for each of the given functions.

$f(x)=\{\begin{array}{l}1,x\lt 1 \\ x,x\ge 1\end{array},x=1$

For the following exercises, use the limit definition of derivative to show that the derivative does not exist at $x=a$ for each of the given functions.

$f(x)=\frac{|x|}{x},x=0$

answer.solution: The derivative at $0$ is $\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{f(x)-f(0)}{x-0},$ which needs $f$ to be defined on an open interval containing $0.$ Here $f(0)=\frac{|0|}{0}$ is undefined, so the difference quotient cannot be formed and $f^{\prime}(0)$ does not exist. Even if $f(0)$ were given some value $c,$ the quotient would be $\frac{1-c}{x}$ for $x\gt 0$ and $\frac{-1-c}{x}$ for $x\lt 0,$ and no choice of $c$ makes both one-sided limits finite and equal, so the limit still would not exist.

exercises.prompt:
Two vehicles start out traveling side by side along a straight road. Their position functions, shown in the following graph, are given by $s=f(t)$ and $s=g(t),$ where $s$ is measured in feet and $t$ is measured in seconds.

a. Which vehicle has traveled farther at $t=2$ seconds?

b. What is the approximate velocity of each vehicle at $t=3$ seconds?

c. Which vehicle is traveling faster at $t=4$ seconds?

d. What is true about the positions of the vehicles at $t=4$ seconds?

answer.solution: a. The vehicle represented by $f(t),$ because it has traveled $2$ feet, whereas $g(t)$ has traveled $1$ foot. b. The velocity of $f(t)$ is constant at $1$ ft/s, while the velocity of $g(t)$ is approximately $2$ ft/s. c. The vehicle represented by $g(t),$ with a velocity of approximately $4$ ft/s. d. Both have traveled $4$ feet in $4$ seconds.

Suppose that $N(x)$ computes the number of gallons of gas used by a vehicle traveling $x$ miles. Suppose the vehicle gets $30$ mpg.

a. Find a mathematical expression for $N(x).$

b. What is $N(100\text{)?}$ Explain the physical meaning.

answer.solution: a. $N(x)=\frac{x}{30}$ b. $\sim 3.3$ gallons. When the vehicle travels $100$ miles, it has used $3.3$ gallons of gas. c. $\frac{1}{30}.$ The rate of gas consumption in gallons per mile that the vehicle is achieving after having traveled $100$ miles.
